review_title: Influenza vaccines for preventing cardiovascular disease
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of influenza vaccination compared with placebo or no treatment in participants with or without cardiovascular disease, assessing cardiovascular death or non‐fatal cardiovascular events.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset labels 1.0 and 0.5 count as INCLUDE; 0.0 counts as EXCLUDE

studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in adults ≥60 years, but the outcomes assessed are influenza efficacy (culture-confirmed influenza), safety, and immunogenicity only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed as outcomes.

studies.study_title: The efficacy of influenza vaccination in elderly individuals. A randomized double‐blind placebo‐controlled trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly individuals, but the outcomes are serological influenza, clinical influenza, and self-reported influenza only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of H5N1 pre-pandemic vaccine vs placebo, but outcomes are immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, safety, and lot consistency only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Influenza vaccination reduces cardiovascular events in patients with acute coronary syndrome
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized PROBE study of influenza vaccine vs no treatment in patients with acute coronary syndrome (CVD population). The primary endpoint was a composite of major cardiovascular events including death, hospitalization from ACS, hospitalization from heart failure, and hospitalization from stroke. This meets all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: A rapid immune response to 2009 influenza a(H1N1) vaccines in adults: a randomized, double‐blind, controlled trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT comparing different dosages/formulations of H1N1 influenza vaccines, but outcomes are immunogenicity (seroprotection rates) and safety only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Is influenza vaccination cost effective for healthy people between ages 65 and 74 years? A randomised controlled trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in healthy people aged 65-74 years (specifically excluding those with chronic heart disease). Outcomes are influenza diagnosis and cost-effectiveness indicators. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed as outcomes.

studies.study_title: Antibody response to influenza vaccine in coronary artery disease: a substudy of the FLUCAD study
studies.predicted_reason: This is a substudy of the FLUCAD RCT focusing only on antibody response (immunogenicity) to influenza vaccine in patients with coronary artery disease. While the parent FLUCAD study assessed cardiovascular outcomes, this specific substudy only reports on humoral immune response, not cardiovascular death or events.

studies.study_title: Effect of influenza and pneumococcal vaccines in elderly persons in years of low influenza activity
studies.predicted_reason: This is an observational prospective cohort study, not a randomized controlled trial. It compares vaccinated vs unvaccinated individuals from administrative databases. While it mentions cardiac failure hospitalizations, the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.

studies.study_title: An open‐label comparison of the immunogenicity and tolerability of intranasal and intramuscular formulations of virosomal influenza vaccine in healthy adults
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT comparing intranasal vs intramuscular influenza vaccine formulations in healthy adults. Outcomes are immunogenicity (HI antibody titers) and tolerability only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

studies.study_title: High‐dose trivalent influenza vaccine compared to standard dose vaccine in elderly adults: safety, immunogenicity and relative efficacy during the 2009‐2010 season
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT comparing high-dose vs standard-dose influenza vaccine in adults ≥65 years. Outcomes are safety (SAEs), immunogenicity (HAI titers), and relative efficacy against influenza only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Comparison of the safety and immunogenicity of 2 respiratory syncytial virus (rsv) vaccines‐‐nonadjuvanted vaccine or vaccine adjuvanted with alum‐‐given concomitantly with influenza vaccine to high‐risk elderly individuals
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT primarily comparing two RSV vaccine formulations given with influenza vaccine in persons ≥65 years with cardiopulmonary disease. Outcomes are RSV vaccine immunogenicity, safety, and respiratory illnesses. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Lack of effect of influenza and pneumococcal vaccines on anticoagulation by warfarin
studies.predicted_reason: This is a controlled study of influenza vaccine effects on warfarin anticoagulation in 69 warfarin recipients. Outcomes are INR values and anticoagulant control only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

studies.study_title: [Impact of an anti‐flu vaccination strategy for prevention of cardiovascular diseases]
studies.predicted_reason: This is a before-after experimental study with a control group evaluating the impact of a vaccination campaign strategy on vaccination coverage and cardiovascular prevention service coverage. It is not an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo/no treatment, and does not assess cardiovascular death or events as clinical outcomes.

studies.study_title: Influenza vaccination is associated with a reduced risk of stroke
studies.predicted_reason: This is a case-control study (observational design), not a randomized controlled trial. It compares vaccination status between stroke/TIA patients and population controls. While it assesses stroke risk, the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.

studies.study_title: [Secondary prevention of coronary artery disease. Flu vaccinations and new evidence of the role of infection in acute coronary syndromes]
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized single-blind study of influenza vaccination vs control in myocardial infarction patients and PCI patients (CVD population). Primary outcomes include cardiovascular death and a triple composite endpoint of cardiovascular ischemic events. This meets all selection criteria for an RCT assessing cardiovascular outcomes in CVD patients.

studies.study_title: Comparison of two vaccination programmes in preventing influenza‐related hospitalization among the elderly during two consecutive seasons
studies.predicted_reason: This is an ecological study comparing two different vaccination programme strategies (risk disease-based vs age-based) at the population level across municipalities. It is not an individual-level RCT. While it mentions cardiovascular hospitalizations, the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.

studies.study_title: Immune response to influenza vaccination in community‐dwelling Chinese elderly persons

studies.study_title: Influenza vaccination and vitamin K antagonist treatment: a placebo‐controlled, randomized, double‐blind crossover study

While thrombotic events are mentioned, the study focuses on coagulation parameters rather than cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events as primary outcomes.

studies.study_title: Safety of a trivalent live attenuated intranasal influenza vaccine, FluMist, administered in addition to parenteral trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine to seniors with chronic medical conditions
